title: Coram / Wincoram
summary: Coram is represented here with the Wincoram and Winnecoram forms, tied to a Brookhaven place-name and a 1677 record of a pond in the woods.
introduction_content: Wincoram is treated as a cross-reference to Coram. The related forms include Winnecoram and appear in Brookhaven place-name records.
history_content: The name is associated with Coram in Brookhaven and with a recorded pond in the woods. The exact historic pond location has not been identified.
translation_content:
The cross-referenced Coram entry gives the sense as "a valley" or "low country."

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names, as scholars such as Keith Basso have noted, are more than just nominal labels: they describe places and embed them in rich cultural geographies imbued with history, memory, and the knowledge required to live on the land.”

— Canadian Mountain Assessment, Mountain place names (2025), chapter 3.2.3
preservation_content: Keeping Wincoram with Coram preserves the alternate spelling without creating a duplicate record for the same place-name tradition.
whereintheworld_content: Approximate blue/general placement in modern Coram, Brookhaven town. Coordinates mark a modern location, not the exact historic pond named in older sources.
